set.containers.desc: Local addresses and HTTPS for your containers
ctr.title: Containers
ctr.offline: Docker isn't running rn. Start it and NoCapOS hooks right back up.
ctr.search: Search name, image, project, port or address
ctr.sort.name: Sort: Name
ctr.none: Nothing here yet. Grab an app from the App Store and it pops up here.
ctr.killMsg: Kill stops it instantly, no time to save or shut down clean.
ctr.proj.stopMsg: All of its containers stop. Start them again whenever.
ctr.proj.removeMsg: Its containers get removed. Volumes and folders stay put. A saved stack keeps its compose file, so you can bring it back.
ctr.proj.stackStarted: {name} is on it, check Stacks for the play-by-play
ctr.sizeHint: What the container wrote to disk
ctr.editStack: Part of {name}: edit its compose file
ctr.updateHint: Download the image again and recreate if it changed
ctr.updateMsg: NoCapOS grabs {image} again. If there's a fresher one, the container gets rebuilt with it, settings and data kept.
ctr.removeFolders: Folders from the server that it used are never touched.
ctr.removeVolumesToo: Also delete its volumes (anything only in those volumes is gone for good)
ctr.localNone: None yet: it needs a web port, or local addresses are off in Settings
ctr.webHint: Containers on a macvlan or ipvlan network open at their own address on their own. Set one here when the app sits behind a reverse proxy or a name like https://media.home.lan.
ctr.envHint: Anything that looks like a password, token or key stays hidden. Edit the container to change values.
ctr.hostNet: Uses the server's own network (host mode).
ctr.cmd.hint: Run one command inside the container (sh -c, up to a minute). For anything longer, open a full terminal.
ctr.cmd.notRunning: Start the container to run commands in it.
ctr.cmd.label: Command
ctr.files.badName: {name} can't be uploaded with that name
ctr.files.badPath: That path doesn't work: start with / and no ..
ctr.files.truncated: Big folder: only the first part is shown.
ctr.files.binary: It's a binary file: no preview, but you can download it.
ctr.files.previewCut: Only the first 1 MB is shown.
ctr.img.untagMsg: Only this name goes; the image stays under its other names.
ctr.img.removeMsg: The image gets deleted from this server. You can download it again anytime.
ctr.img.pruneMsg: {n} images no container uses get deleted ({size}). You can download them again later.
ctr.vol.removeMsg: Everything in it is gone for good.
ctr.vol.pruneMsg: Anonymous volumes no container uses get deleted, data and all.
ctr.vol.pruneNamed: Named ones too ({n} unused in total): their data is gone for good
ctr.dev.hint: USB and serial gadgets plugged into this server (Zigbee sticks, 3D printers, UPS cables…). Attaching one rebuilds the container with --device.
ctr.dev.none: No USB or serial devices plugged in.
ctr.dev.flagHint: What the container gets: the stable name on the server, then the name inside
ctr.dev.attachHint: You'll see the changes before anything happens. Containers in a stack get devices from their compose file.
ctr.dev.editorNote: Adding the device {flag}. Review and apply to rebuild the container with it.
ctr.net.disconnectMsg: It can't reach the other containers on that network anymore.
ctr.spec.limitsHint: Limits keep one container from hogging the whole server. Too tight and the app may crash or slow down.
ctr.spec.readOnlyNote: Safer: the app can only write to its volumes and folders. Some apps need to write elsewhere and won't start.
ctr.spec.privilegedNote: Big risk: the container gets full access to the server, like root. Only turn it on if the app really needs it.
ctr.spec.capsNote: Extra powers for the container. Add only what the app's docs ask for.
ctr.spec.capsHighRisk: Heads up: one of these is almost as strong as privileged mode.
ctr.spec.devicesHint: Devices from the server (e.g. /dev/dri for a GPU, or a serial port)
ctr.la.title: Local addresses
ctr.la.hint: Every container with a web page gets a name on your home network, like http://media.nocap.local. Only devices on your network can open them.
ctr.la.trustHint: Install NoCapOS's certificate on your devices once and every https:// local address just works. It can only vouch for names under nocap.local, nothing else.
ctr.la.noHttps: This server doesn't serve HTTPS right now, so local addresses open over http://.
ctr.la.caHint: nocapos-local-ca.crt: open it on each device and mark it trusted
ctr.la.notAnnounced: Not announced yet: turn on the Shield DNS blocker, or install Avahi, so devices find these names
ctr.la.empty: No running container has a web port yet.
ctr.la.src.label: {name}, its chosen name
ctr.la.customHint: Add these labels to a container to pick its name and which port opens. Lowercase letters, numbers and dashes, up to 3 parts.
